correctness.rationale: For a complete bipartite one-dimensional simplicial input graph, an oriented matching incidence v→u is selected precisely when u is its unique earlier neighbor in a total vertex order. The precedence inequalities restrict each maximal face to pure P_b and Q_a simplices or mixed X_(a,b), Y_(a,b). Each generating facet is realized by a concrete order. Relative-to-vertices descending free-face collapses of each U_b and V_a are valid globally because overlaps consist only of isolated shared vertices. The remaining connected graph has 2mn vertices and 4mn-m-n edges, hence wedge^(2mn-m-n+1) S1. The integral equivariant Mayer-Vietoris exact sequence gives kernel of two signed incidence copies Z[A×B]→Z[A]⊕Z[B], and the rational character 2f(σ)f(τ)-f(σ)-f(τ)+1; part swaps trace 1 when m=n. Fresh enumeration of all (m+n)! orders for (3,3),(3,4),(4,4) exactly matched the proposed entire face sets and Euler counts, and fresh 72 signed S3×S3 automorphism Lefschetz checks (including swaps) all agreed. These finite tests corroborate the all-parameter facet/collapse proof.
